source.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Prepare the fixed SOURCE FRAME for an eight-angle turntable of this exact approved cobalt-blue ceramic mug. Edit the input reference non-destructively: keep its exact mug design, cylindrical body and slightly tapered foot, deep cobalt-blue speckled glossy glaze, rim, large D-shaped handle, physical proportions and material identity. Keep the handle to SCREEN RIGHT in the same readable side-on orientation as the source; this defines angle 0 of the rotation. Change ONLY framing and normalize the studio setup: the cylindrical BODY's vertical axis must be at exactly 50% of the square canvas width, even though the handle makes the total silhouette asymmetric. Reduce the mug enough to leave space for the handle on BOTH sides in subsequent views. Main cylindrical body approximately 48% of canvas width and 60% of canvas height, with its base at 85% canvas height and top rim around 25%; retain the input's modest downward camera elevation, natural perspective and visible empty interior. Do not center the combined body-plus-handle silhouette. Keep the full product and handle comfortably inside all image edges with at least 6% margin. Pure white #FFFFFF seamless floor and background outside localized shadow. Fixed large softbox above CAMERA LEFT, brightest highlight on the body's left surface, realistic darker right surface, and soft neutral-gray contact/cast shadow toward SCREEN RIGHT. Warm-neutral white balance. No props, coffee, steam, saucer, hands, text, brands, watermarks, panels or borders. Output ONE high-resolution square 1254 by 1254 catalog photograph. This frame is the geometry, camera, framing, lighting and floor baseline reference for all subsequent rotations.

execution: Seven independent angle edits from the single normalized source. No rotated output used to generate another. JPEG format conversion only.

assets.prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Create one frame of an eight-angle product turntable of the EXACT cobalt-blue ceramic mug in the reference. The reference is the fixed product-identity, framing, camera and lighting anchor for ALL frames. Rotate only the mug as a single rigid object about its vertical cylindrical-body axis to the requested angle. Keep the exact same body width and height, taper, rounded rim, slightly narrower beige foot, cobalt speckled glossy glaze, D-shaped handle dimensions and attachment heights, empty interior, camera elevation and focal length. Do not redesign the handle or mug. Keep the cylindrical BODY's center, top rim and base at the same pixel positions as the reference, independent of handle position: no automatic reframing or centering of the combined body-plus-handle silhouette, no zoom, no orbiting the camera. Maintain full product visibility. The light is fixed ABOVE CAMERA LEFT: broad highlight on screen-left of cylindrical body, darker screen-right body, consistent white balance and exposure. Specular highlights must NOT rotate around the cylindrical body with the handle. The soft neutral-gray floor shadow must always extend SCREEN RIGHT. Pure white #FFFFFF seamless background and floor outside local shadow. Recompute realistic handle occlusion, perspective and self-shadow for the requested orientation. Photorealistic catalog image, detailed ceramic glaze. Do not horizontally flip the reference or another frame. No text, brand, graphics, props, coffee, steam, saucer, hands, labels, borders or montage. Output ONE square 1254 by 1254 photograph matching the reference's framing and aspect ratio. Requested angle: 45 degrees. Rotate the mug 45 degrees so its handle moves from screen right toward the FAR/REAR RIGHT of the mug, partly behind the right edge. The handle's opening becomes visibly narrower from foreshortening, and its attachment points partly occlude behind the body. Keep the handle outside the upper-right outline enough to recognize the intermediate orientation. This is halfway between the reference's full handle-on-right view and a handle-directly-behind view.
